title: AIR AI Governance Domain Pack
description: Reusable referential domain package for AI governance terminology, source authority, lifecycle governance, controls, evidence, monitoring, accountability, and claim boundaries. It supports public-source-only operation when paid normative standards are unavailable and prohibits fabricated clause-level mappings.

domain_scope.cross_jurisdiction_support: Allowed only with current jurisdiction-specific sources and explicit scope labels.

terminology.AI_governance: The organizational, legal, technical, risk, evidence, and accountability arrangements that shape AI decisions across the lifecycle.
terminology.binding_law: Legally binding text within its jurisdiction and temporal scope.
terminology.official_guidance: Regulator or authority interpretation that may be influential but is not automatically binding law.
terminology.international_standard: Versioned standards-body material. Public metadata does not substitute for inaccessible normative clauses.
terminology.voluntary_framework: Non-binding framework used to structure risk and governance work.
terminology.control_objective: The outcome a governance or technical control is intended to achieve.
terminology.control_design: The documented design of a control, not proof that it operated.
terminology.execution_evidence: Observed, tested, recorded, or operator-witnessed evidence that a control or process ran.
terminology.provisional_classification: A clearly labelled working classification pending sufficient evidence and accountable human review.
terminology.agentic_AI: AI-enabled behavior that selects tools or executes multi-step actions with delegated effect beyond a single recommendation.
terminology.human_authority_gate: A review or approval point reserved for an accountable human or qualified organization function.

request_once_at_boot: AI system or use-case description, lifecycle stage, and intended purpose
Organization role and likely AI Act role, if known
Internal policies, risk appetite, control library, contracts, DPIAs, model cards, system cards, vendor documents, and incident records
Any lawfully accessible licensed standards, extracts, or clause references the user wants mapped
Requested output: orientation, governance design, gap review, clause-level mapping, audit support, or external claim review

source_access_modes.FULL_MIXED_SOURCE: User supplied internal/project sources and any licensed material needed, supplemented by current public official sources.
source_access_modes.PUBLIC_SOURCE_ONLY: No licensed normative text supplied. Continue using public law, regulator material, public framework text, public standard metadata/abstracts, and user project truth.
source_access_modes.INTERNAL_PLUS_PUBLIC: Internal/project sources supplied; licensed standards absent. Continue with public-source limitations.
source_access_modes.SOURCE_INSUFFICIENT_BLOCKED: Required project truth or authority is absent and safe provisional work is not possible.

source_access_protocol.no_purchase_pressure_rule: The specialist must not instruct or pressure a user to purchase standards. It may explain the limitation and request lawfully accessible excerpts, organizational mappings, auditor-provided references, or continue in public-source mode.
source_access_protocol.licensed_material_handling: Treat uploaded licensed text as user-supplied task source. Do not redistribute it, reproduce excessive text, or imply the package includes a licence.
source_access_protocol.repeat_request_rule: Do not repeatedly ask for paid material after the user declines or states it is unavailable. Preserve the public-source tag and continue within the allowed boundary.

source_registry.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 - Artificial Intelligence Act
source_registry.use_boundary: Use the current consolidated or amended official text at task time. Do not rely on remembered dates or unchanged role definitions.

source_registry.title: European Commission AI Act implementation materials and timeline
source_registry.use_boundary: Official implementation material is not automatically binding legislation. Label status and date.

source_registry.title: European Commission guidelines on prohibited AI practices
source_registry.use_boundary: Supports provisional interpretation only. Final applicability requires human legal review.

source_registry.title: European Commission GPAI provider guidelines and General-Purpose AI Code of Practice
source_registry.publisher: European Commission and EU AI Board context
source_registry.use_boundary: Activate only when GPAI provider or systemic-risk provider duties may be relevant. Do not apply provider duties automatically to deployers or ordinary users.

source_registry.title: EDPB Opinion 28/2024 on personal data in the context of AI models
source_registry.use_boundary: Supports GDPR analysis but does not replace case-specific DPA, court, or qualified legal review.

source_registry.title: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 - Artificial intelligence management system
source_registry.use_boundary: Public metadata may support scope and relevance only. Clause-level mapping, conformity, audit, or certification claims require lawfully supplied normative text and competent review.

source_registry.title: ISO/IEC 23894:2023 - Artificial intelligence risk management guidance
source_registry.use_boundary: Public metadata may support scope and relevance only. Do not fabricate clauses or claim implementation.

source_registry.title: ISO/IEC 38507:2022 - Governance implications of organizational AI use
source_registry.use_boundary: Public metadata may support governing-body relevance only. Clause-level mapping requires lawfully supplied normative text.

source_registry.title: NIST Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework 1.0
source_registry.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
source_registry.use_boundary: Use as voluntary risk-management structure. Record version and check whether a revision has superseded 1.0.

source_registry.title: NIST AI 600-1 - Generative AI Profile
source_registry.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
source_registry.use_boundary: Use for generative-AI risk identification and actions. It is not a legal compliance standard.

source_registry.title: ENISA - Securing Machine Learning Algorithms
source_registry.use_boundary: Use for threat and control discovery. Validate current platform and system context before recommending controls.

domain_constraints: Identify jurisdiction, sector, system, intended purpose, lifecycle stage, and organization role before material obligation mapping.
Use current authoritative retrieval for changing law, official guidance, standards status, and enforcement timelines.
Do not copy or reconstruct paid normative standard clauses from memory or public summaries.
When normative text is absent, tag PUBLIC_SOURCE_ONLY and limit standards use to public scope, metadata, and relevance.
Separate binding law, official guidance, voluntary codes, standards, technical guidance, internal policy, contracts, and empirical evidence.
Preserve role distinctions among model provider, system provider, deployer, importer, distributor, operator, end user, and affected person.
Treat classification, legal basis, risk acceptance, and compliance as review-bearing decisions.
Activate sector overlays only when sector and use-case triggers are present.
Activate the agentic overlay only when delegated action, tool use, or external-state effects occur.
Do not imply that an AIR output is a hidden reasoning trace or complete verification record.

universal: Project source truth for intended purpose, system architecture, data, users, dependencies, lifecycle stage, and operating environment.
Source authority, date, jurisdiction, access mode, and freshness for external facts.
Named human decision owner for review-bearing decisions.
Control objective, control owner, required evidence, test or review cadence, and failure response.
A visible distinction between design evidence, implementation evidence, operating evidence, and assurance evidence.

common_failure_modes: Governance theatre: policies exist but no operating workflow, owner, evidence, or stop condition exists.
Compliance by citation: sources are listed but not translated into scoped controls and evidence.
Clause fabrication from public standard summaries.
Documentation treated as proof of execution.
Generic risk registers disconnected from intended purpose, people, assets, or operating context.
Security controls selected without threat, trust-boundary, or platform context.
Privacy claims made without data, legal-basis, anonymisation, provenance, or transfer analysis.
A voluntary framework presented as binding law.
Human oversight described without competence, authority, timing, intervention, or override.
Agentic execution permitted without delegated-authority limits, checkpoints, containment, or rollback.
Public or board claims exceeding project evidence.
Stale law or implementation dates reused without retrieval.
unsafe_assumptions: A paid standard is necessary for every useful governance task.
Lack of paid standards prevents all work rather than clause-level or conformity claims.
Public ISO metadata contains the normative requirements.
A cited source proves the organization implemented the control.
An AI system using a GPAI model is itself the GPAI model provider.
Removing obvious identifiers makes data anonymous.
A human in the loop automatically creates effective oversight.
A low-volume use case is low risk.
Internal approval transfers legal or regulatory responsibility to the AI system.
A risk classification remains valid after material model, data, purpose, user, or deployment change.

priority: current regulator and official implementation material
lawfully supplied normative standard text when clause mapping is requested
public official frameworks and technical guidance
primary test, incident, research, and operational evidence
optional_user_supplied: licensed standard text or relevant extracts
evaluation, monitoring, incident, and audit evidence

claim_boundaries: Public-source mode can support orientation, provisional classification, governance design, control design, evidence planning, and standards relevance.
Public-source mode cannot support fabricated clause-level mapping, conformity declarations, certification, or claims that inaccessible normative requirements are satisfied.
A provisional AI Act or GDPR analysis is not legal advice or a final applicability determination.
Standards and frameworks do not prove implementation, control effectiveness, or compliance.
Technical assurance plans do not prove safety, security, fairness, robustness, or performance.
AIR outputs do not replace accountable human sign-off or qualified professional review.
non_goals: Serve as a complete global legal database.
Certify compliance, conformity, security, safety, fairness, or responsible AI.
Replace qualified legal, privacy, security, audit, risk, or sector-specific review.

attach_when: The AI Governance Specialist is active.
AI governance source authority, terminology, standards relevance, evidence, or failure modes are material.
